mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 3% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO above 2% and a fall in HOUST below 1950 (in thousands of units) over two months signals supply chain inflation with declining housing starts, which compresses corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 2% AND HOUST < 1950 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% while CPIAUCSL rises above 3% YoY signals a policy-lag environment where monetary easing fails to offset inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% signals accelerated savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS above 2% and UNRATE above 6% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market with wage inflation, which increases input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 2% AND UNRATE > 6% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly decline in GDPC1 for three consecutive quarters signals a deepening economic contraction, which reliably predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such quarters.
